newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan opposition bars president's keynote address.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan opposition bars president's keynote address.

text.p: Opposition politicians incensed over the Taiwan government's crime-fighting record on Tuesday prevented President Lee Teng-hui from delivering a keynote address to the National Assembly.

"We cannot continue today's agenda. We will adjourn today and continue tomorrow," Frederick Chien, speaker of the largely ceremonial National Assembly, said after an opposition filibuster halted the proceedings.

Opposition assembly members wearing white and yellow robes bearing protest slogans took advantage of procedural rules allowing them to make a string of speeches from the National Assembly podium, effectively preventing Lee from speaking.

Each demanded that Lee apologise for a series of horrific, unsolved crimes, most recently a school girl's kidnap and murder, that have shaken public confidence in the government's ability to maintain law and order.
The president, whose annual address had already been made public in draft form, left the assembly hall without comment.

Across town in parliament, lawmakers were expected to vote on Tuesday on a non-binding resolution urging Lee to undertake a sweeping reshuffle and sack Premier Lien, who Lee has been grooming as his successor.
